articles.title: Clube Poliglota IFSertãoPE abre 106 vagas para cursos de idiomas | G1
articles.standfirst: Interessados podem se inscrever gratuitamente até 29 de outubro para participar de encontros de conversação em inglês, espanhol e francês, além de um grupo de estudos de francês.
articles.summary: O Clube Poliglota do IFSertãoPE Petrolina oferece 106 vagas gratuitas para conversação em inglês, espanhol e francês. Inscrições abertas até 29 de outubro para toda a comunidade.
articles.body:
IFSertãoPE Campus Petrolina Zona Rural — Foto: Emerson Rocha / g1 Petrolina

O campus Petrolina Zona Rural do Instituto Federal do Sertão Pernambucano (IFSertãoPE) está com inscrições abertas para novos participantes do Clube Poliglota. O projeto de extensão oferece atividades gratuitas para a prática de conversação em inglês, espanhol e francês, além de um grupo de estudos voltado ao aprendizado da língua francesa.

Ao todo, são oferecidas 106 vagas, distribuídas entre quatro modalidades: 30 para conversação em inglês, 30 para conversação em espanhol, 30 para conversação em francês e 16 para o grupo de estudos de francês.

Metade das vagas é destinada à comunidade interna do IFSertãoPE, incluindo servidores, estudantes e trabalhadores terceirizados de todos os campi. A outra metade é reservada ao público externo.

As inscrições podem ser feitas até o dia 29 de outubro, exclusivamente por meio de formulários eletrônicos. Os candidatos devem escolher o link correspondente à categoria de participação, comunidade interna ou externa, e à modalidade desejada.

Os formulários de inscrição estão disponíveis no Edital (clique aqui). Os candidatos convocados para os encontros de conversação também deverão enviar um vídeo gravado no idioma escolhido.

Os encontros de conversação e o grupo de estudos de francês serão realizados semanalmente, de forma virtual, pela plataforma Google Meet, a partir do dia 17 de novembro. Nas atividades de conversação, os participantes discutirão temas como filmes, músicas, clima, viagens, livros, tecnologia e rotina, além de utilizar recursos didáticos para estimular a interação.

Já o grupo de estudos de francês contará com textos, vídeos e áudios para auxiliar no aprendizado da gramática, no aprimoramento da pronúncia e na ampliação do vocabulário.

articles.title: Macapá e Santana: R$ 7,6 mi para merenda da agricultura familiar | G1
articles.standfirst: Verba vai financiar a compra de alimentos regionais em 2026. A medida atende cerca de 81 mil estudantes de 183 unidades.
articles.summary: Com R$ 7,6 milhões, a merenda escolar em Macapá e Santana terá alimentos da agricultura familiar para 81 mil alunos de 183 unidades em 2026.
articles.body:
Escolas estaduais de Macapá e Santana terão R$ 7,6 milhões da agricultura familiar na merenda. — Foto: Márcio Bezerra/Seed

A merenda de 183 escolas estaduais em Macapá e Santana receberá R$ 7,6 milhões em produtos da agricultura familiar em 2026. Os contratos foram firmados pela Secretaria de Estado da Educação (Seed) para abastecer a rede pública de ensino com alimentos regionais.

A medida atende a uma diretriz do Programa Nacional de Alimentação Escolar (Pnae), que utiliza repasses federais para comprar alimentos de produtores locais.

Desde a metade de 2024, a totalidade dessa verba em Macapá e Santana vem sendo direcionada para produtores da região, somando mais de R$ 8,4 milhões no período.

Atualmente, 18 itens são adquiridos da agricultura familiar por meio de chamadas públicas. O cardápio inclui frutas, hortaliças, legumes, farinha de mandioca, polpas de frutas e açaí.

Na Escola Estadual Antônio Cordeiro Pontes, no Centro de Macapá , a merenda servida na última quinta-feira (22) acompanhou arroz temperado, carne moída com legumes, couve, cenoura, banana e farinha.

Para os estudantes, o cardápio diversificado impacta diretamente a rotina escolar.

"A comida da escola é muito boa e tem bastante variedade. A gente tem frutas, verduras e refeições diferentes durante a semana. É muito bom poder estudar e ter uma alimentação preparada aqui para nós", conta a aluna do 2º ano, Dominic Rodrigues.

Estudante Dominic Rodrigues, do segundo ano. — Foto: Márcio Bezerra/Seed

Recursos estaduais complementam verba federal

Além da verba federal do Pnae, o estado repassa verbas do Programa de Alimentação Escolar (Proem) diretamente para as unidades de ensino. O montante é utilizado para comprar outros itens básicos de consumo que não vêm da agricultura familiar, como carnes e grãos.

Enquanto a Seed coordena as chamadas públicas para os produtores locais, cada unidade escolar faz a compra direta dos demais alimentos com o orçamento do programa estadual.

Atendimento a estudantes indígenas e quilombolas

Em julho de 2026, uma chamada pública de R$ 718,9 mil foi lançada para comprar 33 itens da agricultura familiar voltados a comunidades tradicionais.

A medida atende cerca de 7,4 mil alunos de 77 escolas em áreas indígenas e quilombolas. O cardápio diferenciado inclui produtos locais como pescado, açaí, bacaba, farinhas, frutas e verduras.

Para 2026, o abastecimento envolve 16 contratos divididos entre duas cooperativas, quatro associações e dez agricultores individuais. A estimativa é atender 468 produtores rurais diretos e cerca de 2 mil fornecedores e familiares na região.

Attafex-San : Associação dos Trabalhadores e Trabalhadoras Rurais da Agricultura Familiar e do Extrativismo de Santana ;

Paif : Associação dos Produtores Agroextrativistas da Ilha do Franco (Arquipélago do Bailique);

Amacrep : Associação de Moradores e Agricultores da Comunidade da Ressaca da Pedreira;

Acipol : Associação dos Agricultores Familiares e Aquicultores do Polo Hortifrutigranjeiro da Fazendinha ( Macapá .

articles.title: Japão vai simular ataques hackers com IA após falha no PHP tirar sites do ar em vários países | G1
articles.standfirst: Falhas graves na linguagem de programação PHP, usada em grande parte da internet, provocaram milhões de tentativas de invasão e levaram empresas e órgãos públicos de vários países a suspender serviços, incluindo alertas de emergência no Japão.
articles.summary: Falhas graves na linguagem de programação PHP, usada em grande parte da internet, provocaram milhões de tentativas de invasão.
articles.body:
O Japão anunciou nesta sexta-feira (23) que criará uma equipe para simular ataques cibernéticos com inteligência artificial (IA) e identificar falhas em sistemas tecnológicos.

A medida ocorre em meio a uma onda de ataques que levou empresas e órgãos públicos de vários países a tirar sites do ar para se proteger de vulnerabilidades na linguagem de programação PHP , usada em grande parte da internet.

Nesta semana, milhões de tentativas de invasão foram registradas após a divulgação de falhas graves no PHP , levando operadores de sites a reforçar a segurança ou suspender temporariamente seus sistemas.

Um dos efeitos da crise foi a suspensão, pela SoftBank, terceira maior operadora de telefonia móvel do Japão, de seu sistema de alertas de emergência para celulares.

Com mais de 30 milhões de clientes de smartphones, a empresa informou nesta sexta-feira que o serviço ficará indisponível durante a manutenção para corrigir uma falha no PHP.

Com isso, os usuários deixarão de receber alertas antecipados de terremotos, avisos de tsunamis e informações sobre desastres e evacuações . A SoftBank afirmou, porém, que os clientes ainda poderão receber alertas de terremotos por outros serviços, como um aplicativo de sua empresa Yahoo .

O Japão é frequentemente atingido por desastres naturais e está entre os países mais sujeitos a terremotos do mundo. O tufão Champi também se aproxima de Okinawa, a província mais ao sul do país.

"Um ataque pode ser bem-sucedido ao encontrar apenas uma brecha. Por isso, é importante mudarmos nossa mentalidade e pensar sob a perspectiva do invasor", afirmou o ministro japonês da Indústria, Ryosei Akazawa, nesta sexta-feira, à Reuters.

"Os responsáveis pela defesa também precisam usar a inteligência artificial e agir de forma proativa, mantendo-se um passo à frente", acrescentou.

Nobuo Miwa, presidente da empresa de segurança cibernética S&J Corp, sediada em Tóquio, avaliou que a resposta do governo foi lenta demais.

"É como tentar enfrentar um homem-bomba com uma lança de bambu", afirmou.

Falhas no PHP tiram serviços do ar em vários países

As interrupções emergenciais registradas nesta semana, de Tóquio a Helsinque, afetaram serviços bancários, aéreos, ferroviários, tributários e governamentais. O episódio se tornou um dos testes mais expressivos para ferramentas de programação criadas há décadas e que sustentam o funcionamento da internet.

No Japão, empresas como a corretora Nomura, o grupo financeiro Mitsubishi UFJ, a companhia aérea ANA e a operadora ferroviária JR East suspenderam temporariamente alguns serviços on-line como medida de emergência.

O Ministério das Finanças, a Agência Nacional de Impostos e a Agência Meteorológica do Japão também interromperam parte de seus serviços pela internet.

Nesta sexta-feira, a JR East informou que alguns serviços de empresas do grupo haviam voltado a funcionar. Os demais seriam restabelecidos após a confirmação de que estavam seguros.

Já a fabricante de tintas Nippon Paint afirmou ter instalado uma atualização de segurança por precaução e informou que seu site estava novamente no ar.

Para Eva Chen, presidente-executiva da empresa de segurança cibernética Trend Micro, os invasores provavelmente estão mirando empresas japonesas por causa dos registros detalhados que elas mantêm . Segundo ela, a inteligência artificial também reduziu a barreira do idioma, facilitando ataques contra essas organizações.

Chen afirmou ainda que o Japão se tornou excessivamente confiante na segurança de sua infraestrutura tecnológica existente.

Especialistas em segurança cibernética alertam que a inteligência artificial está ajudando criminosos a automatizar tarefas, desde a busca por falhas em programas até a criação de campanhas de phishing — golpes que tentam enganar pessoas para obter informações confidenciais, como senhas.

Com isso, os crimes digitais podem se tornar mais rápidos, baratos e difíceis de detectar.

Os desenvolvedores do PHP divulgaram correções na quarta-feira (21) para vulnerabilidades que estavam presentes no programa havia anos e foram descobertas com o auxílio da inteligência artificial. Eles recomendaram que os usuários atualizassem o software imediatamente.

A linguagem PHP é um conjunto de instruções usado para desenvolver sites e aplicações na internet. Uma vulnerabilidade é uma falha que pode ser explorada por invasores para acessar sistemas, roubar informações ou interromper serviços.

As atualizações de segurança corrigem esses problemas e reduzem o risco de ataques.

articles.title: Campo Grande celebra Dia da Animação com 3 dias de filmes nacionais e  | G1
articles.standfirst: A programação inclui curtas-metragens brasileiros e estrangeiros, com sessões infantis nos dias 23 e 24 de outubro e mostra nacionais e internacionais no dia 28.
articles.summary: A programação inclui curtas-metragens brasileiros e estrangeiros, com sessões infantis nos dias 23 e 24 de outubro e mostra nacionais e internacionais no dia 28.
articles.body:
Campo Grande celebra o Dia Internacional da Animação, em 28 de outubro, com sessões gratuitas de curtas-metragens nacionais e internacionais. A capital está entre as cidades brasileiras que recebem a mostra nacional de curtas.

Em Campo Grande, a programação ocorre em três locais: no Núcleo Humanitário da Nhanhá, no Coletivo Arte em Movimento e na Escola Estadual Adventor Divino de Almeida, com atividades entre sexta-feira (23) e quarta-feira (28).

As sessões incluem animações para crianças e filmes destinados a públicos de outras faixas etárias. A programação infantil aborda temas como amizade, generosidade, sonhos e afeto. Já as mostras nacional e internacional apresentam histórias que tratam de questões ambientais, memórias, conflitos sociais e relações humanas.

Programação do Dia Internacional da Animação?

A mostra de curtas-metragens do Dia Internacional da Animação (DIA) foi criada para divulgar filmes de animação e ampliar o acesso da população a esse tipo de produção audiovisual. No Brasil, o evento reúne exibições em cidades de todas as regiões do país, com entrada gratuita.

A mostra principal ocorre simultaneamente em diferentes localidades no dia 28 de outubro.

Em 2026, o evento chega à sua 23ª edição desde a primeira realização, em 2004, no Sesc Vila Mariana, em São Paulo. A data escolhida para a celebração faz referência à primeira projeção pública de imagens animadas, realizada em 28 de outubro de 1892 pelo francês Charles-Émile Reynaud, no Museu Grévin, em Paris.

Vaca Amarela será um dos fimes exibidos para crianças. — Foto: Divulgação / Dia da Animação

As sessões voltadas ao público infantil têm classificação livre e reúnem histórias sobre amizade, sonhos, convivência e descobertas. A programação inclui a mostra infantil, com curtas como:

Esperança: uma menina negra de 12 anos que sonha em se tornar jogadora profissional de futebol.

O Leão e o Rato: aborda a bondade e mostra como até os menores podem ajudar os outros.

Vaca Amarela: sobre amigos que precisam lidar com uma tempestade.

O Chapéu do Zezéu: produzido por crianças com materiais encontrados na escola e nos quintais.

A Viagem de Tetê: aborda o desmame de forma lúdica para crianças.

As histórias exploram diferentes temas, como a busca por um sonho, a importância da solidariedade, a relação com a natureza, a criatividade e as mudanças na infância. Os filmes vão ser reproduzidos nos seguintes locais:

Endereço: Rua do Comércio, 149, Jardim Nhanhá.

Endereço: Rua João Francisco Damasceno, 1.429.

Filmes produzidos por todo Brasil e pelo mundo também serão exibidos. — Foto: Divulgação/ Dia da Animação

A sessão reúne curtas brasileiros e estrangeiros. A mostra internacional tem classificação indicativa de 12 anos, enquanto a nacional não é recomendada para menores de 14 anos. Confira o local de exibição:

Quarta-feira (28), às 19h — Escola Estadual Adventor Divino de Almeida / Praça Epaminondas Alves Pereira.

Endereço: Avenida Júlio de Castilho, 841, Vila Alba.

Eating Time (Estônia, 2025): acompanha uma senhora que, após uma explosão, chega à oficina de um sapateiro e embarca em uma viagem surreal pelas próprias memórias. Para avançar no tempo, ela precisa literalmente “comer o tempo”.

Carmela (Espanha, 2025): retrata uma mulher que se junta às milícias após a Guerra Civil Espanhola, em uma luta contra o fascismo e pela defesa das liberdades conquistadas durante a Segunda República.

Pintango (Argentina, 2021): mostra Pacho e Mimi, personagens que vivem em uma maquete de animação e tentam superar dificuldades financeiras com um espetáculo de tango para vender seus quadros.

Loop (Argentina/Espanha, 2022): apresenta uma sociedade em que cada pessoa repete continuamente a mesma ação, explorando a repetição na vida cotidiana.

O Coração da Boiúna (Pará, 2026): apresenta a história de uma serpente gigante dos rios amazônicos pelo olhar de Maria Estrela, uma menina de 8 anos. Com a ajuda dos pais, ela reconta a lenda e propõe uma reflexão sobre a consciência ambiental.

Te Vejo Lá (Minas Gerais, 2026): acompanha Violeta e Rosa, que estão prestes a embarcar em uma viagem astral sob a luz da lua cheia.

Entre Folhas e Ventos (Bahia, 2026): conta a história de Jahi, que se fecha no quarto, e de sua gata, Ela, que atravessa folhas, ventos e memórias para reencontrá-lo. A animação aborda cuidado, afeto e permanência.

Mãe da Manhã (Rio Grande do Sul, 2025): apresenta uma criatura faminta que busca alimento durante a noite e mantém um ciclo contínuo.

Peixe Seco e Defumado (Santa Catarina, 2026): retrata a tradição do arrastão da tainha na ilha de São Francisco do Sul e o preparo da cambira, prato típico do litoral, a partir das memórias da pescadora Sirlene.

Como Nasce um Rio (Bahia, 2025): acompanha Ayla em uma jornada por uma paisagem montanhosa, cercada por vegetação e um rio, durante a qual ela explora o ambiente e descobre mais sobre si mesma.

Pária (São Paulo, 2023): mostra uma jovem cercada por pessoas violentas que se conecta com uma garotinha enquanto enfrenta um homem e luta pela própria vida e pelo direito de ocupar seu lugar no mundo.

articles.title: Passagens gratuitas no Pará: eleitores denunciam falta de bilhetes | G1
articles.standfirst: Passageiros relatam negativa de bilhetes e falta de informação em terminais de Belém. Agência reguladora afirma que não há limite para emissão de passagens gratuitas e que empresas devem oferecer viagens extras em caso de alta demanda.
articles.summary: Eleitores denunciam falta de passagens gratuitas no Pará e a Artran reforça que empresas devem garantir o transporte para as eleições sem limite de cotas.
articles.body:
Movimentação no Terminal Rodoviário de Belém — Foto: Elivaldo Pamplona/ O Liberal

Eleitores que precisam viajar para votar no segundo turno das eleições, marcado para domingo (25), denunciam falta de passagens gratuitas, longas filas e dificuldades para obter informações em terminais de Belém , nesta sexta-feira (23). Um passageiro afirma que precisou pagar R$ 150 pela viagem, enquanto outra eleitora diz que não poderá votar por falta de dinheiro.

No Porto Bom Jesus, que atende passageiros com destino a municípios do arquipélago do Marajó, eleitores relataram que não conseguiram retirar os bilhetes gratuitos.

O advogado Rodriano Ribeiro, que vota em Breves , conta que procurou a gratuidade, mas uma atendente informou que a cota de passagens havia se esgotado. Para conseguir viajar, precisou desembolsar R$ 150.

"Não consegui gratuidade porque, quando cheguei para solicitar, a atendente do guichê disse que a cota já tinha expirado. Mas, pelo decreto do governo do estado, não existe cota. Inclusive, tive que comprar passagem no valor de R$ 150", relatou.

A empreendedora Luci Silva também procurou uma passagem gratuita para Curralinho , no Marajó, mas afirma que não conseguiu. Sem condições de pagar pelo deslocamento, ela diz que não poderá votar no domingo.

"Não vou, porque não tenho esse valor neste momento", afirmou.

Segundo a Agência de Regulação e Controle dos Serviços Públicos de Transporte do Pará (Artran), não existe limite para a emissão de passagens gratuitas destinadas ao deslocamento eleitoral. A agência esclareceu que, em caso de excesso de passageiros, as empresas devem organizar viagens extras para garantir o atendimento.

No Porto do Arapari, passageiros enfrentaram filas para retirar bilhetes gratuitos com destino a Barcarena. Segundo relatos, o movimento foi ainda maior durante a manhã.

A autônoma Ângela Vasconcelos tentava conseguir passagens para viajar com o marido e os dois filhos. Sem saber em qual fila deveria aguardar, recebeu orientações para procurar outro ponto de atendimento.

A dona de casa Edenilza Brasil também relatou demora. Segundo ela, as filas estavam ainda maiores no início do dia.

A universitária Laísa Baia procurava uma passagem gratuita para Cametá. Ela conta que decidiu ir ao porto depois que o irmão tentou conseguir o benefício na empresa Boa Esperança e foi informado de que a emissão de bilhetes gratuitos havia sido encerrada.

Apesar das reclamações, alguns passageiros conseguiram retirar as passagens. O estudante Luís Pantoja garantiu os bilhetes de ida e volta para Barcarena e afirmou que a principal dificuldade foi o tempo de espera.

A Artran informou que mantém equipes nos principais terminais rodoviários do estado e no Terminal Hidroviário de Belém para acompanhar a operação. Segundo a agência, eventuais denúncias de recusa da gratuidade serão apuradas, com adoção das medidas cabíveis.

O Tribunal Regional Eleitoral do Pará (TRE-PA) informou que, até esta sexta-feira, não havia registro formal ou processo judicial em tramitação no tribunal sobre descumprimento das regras de gratuidade no transporte intermunicipal durante as eleições de 2026.

O TRE-PA orienta que eleitores que enfrentarem negativa do benefício também podem procurar o Ministério Público ou a Defensoria Pública da União.

A gratuidade no transporte intermunicipal rodoviário e hidroviário está prevista no Decreto Estadual nº 5.715/2026 e vale das 12h desta sexta-feira (23) até as 12h de segunda-feira (26).

Segundo a Artran, o eleitor deve solicitar a passagem no guichê de uma empresa cadastrada e regulada pela agência, apresentando título de eleitor, e-Título ou outro documento físico ou eletrônico que comprove a identidade e o local de votação.

Não é necessário apresentar comprovante de votação ou justificativa do primeiro turno para conseguir a passagem de ida. Para o retorno, são exigidos o comprovante de votação do segundo turno e o bilhete gratuito utilizado na ida.

A agência também esclareceu que não existe prazo de antecedência estabelecido para solicitar as passagens.

Em caso de recusa, o passageiro pode registrar denúncia na Ouvidoria da Artran pelo e-mail ouvidoria@artran.pa.gov.br ou pelo telefone (91) 98418-6173.

articles.title: Alunos saem pelas janelas após ônibus derrapar em ponte em Campos | G1
articles.standfirst: Acidente aconteceu na região de Palmares, próximo à divisa com Cardoso Moreira. Uma escada foi usada para retirar os alunos em segurança.
articles.summary: Acidente aconteceu na região de Palmares, próximo à divisa com Cardoso Moreira. Uma escada foi usada para retirar os alunos em segurança.
articles.body:
Um ônibus que transportava estudantes da rede estadual perdeu a aderência e derrapou em uma ponte de madeira na região de Palmares, distrito de Campos dos Goytacazes , no Norte Fluminense. Como a porta principal ficou inacessível, os estudantes saíram pelas janelas com o auxílio de uma escada. O caso aconteceu nesta quinta-feira (22).

O local fica próximo à divisa com o município de Cardoso Moreira. O coletivo fazia a linha entre Murundu e Cardoso Moreira com alunos matriculados no Colégio Estadual Baltazar Carneiro.

Com o incidente, o ônibus ficou impossibilitado de seguir viagem. A lateral da porta de embarque e desembarque ficou para fora da estrutura da ponte.

Em nota enviada ao g1 , a Prefeitura de Campos dos Goytacazes , por meio da Secretaria Municipal de Agricultura, informou que análises preliminares feitas com base em imagens indicam que o veículo pode ter derrapado devido a uma falha mecânica em uma das rodas. A pasta afirmou que a estrutura da ponte não sofreu danos e declarou que já existe um projeto para o trecho, que foi inserido em um sistema federal para captação de recursos destinados a futuras obras de reforma.

Por sua vez, a Secretaria de Estado de Educação (Seeduc) informou que a situação foi resolvida rapidamente com o transbordo dos estudantes para outro veículo, que os levou até a unidade de ensino. O órgão estadual destacou que mantém diálogo com as famílias dos alunos e que adotará medidas adicionais de segurança para evitar novos episódios semelhantes.

articles.title: Student movement takes Serbia's Vučić to the wire in neck-and-neck election
articles.summary: The Student List has emerged from almost two years of anti-corruption protests to form the biggest challenge to Vučić's rule.
articles.body:
If Sunday's parliamentary elections really are a battle for the heart of Serbia, then who better than a cardiologist to be one of the leading figures in the race.

Ilija Srdanović appears an unlikely opponent for Serbia's long-serving leader, Aleksandar Vučić, arriving for an interview by motorbike sporting a fluorescent yellow jacket emblazoned with pro-student slogans.

He has been selected as top candidate for an opposition movement posing the most serious challenge to Vučić since the Serbian Progressive Party (SNS) entered government in 2012.

The Student List has emerged from almost two years of anti-corruption protests led by young Serbians, outraged by the deaths of 16 people when a railway station's canopy collapsed in Serbia's second city Novi Sad.

What you need to know about Serbia's pivotal election

Instead of running for office themselves, student-led assemblies at the country's university faculties have chosen 250 candidates to stand in the parliamentary election, with Srdanović, professor at Novi Sad University, heading the list.

"It is absolutely normal to stand with my students to help them in their fair struggle," Srdanović told the BBC.

The Student List is up against a Serbian leader who has served successively as deputy prime minister, prime minister and president since 2012. When he called these snap elections last month , he stood down as president to run again for the role of prime minister.

Whatever Vučić's title, there has never been any doubt that he was the man in charge – an image enthusiastically promoted by Serbia's largely uncritical media.

He retains strong support among a significant section of Serbia's population. They view him as a strong leader who stands up for the country's interests. He can also point to significant economic growth over the past decade and numerous improvements in infrastructure.

Vučić has painted the student movement as foreign-backed and seeking to "bring down our state". "Let us always protect and defend it," he told supporters at a final campaign rally.

Just like the protest movement from which it developed, the Student List has no hierarchy or nominated leader. This makes it a proposition unlike any other in Serbia's relatively short democratic history.

Reliable polls are thin on the ground, but analysts are predicting an extremely tight vote.

Ilija Srdanović may head the list of candidates – but he is not the movement's leader and would not necessarily be first choice prime minister if they won.

Srdanović insists that the Student List has a clear vision: "We offer to our citizens the core values of civilised society, which this previous regime has taken away from our citizens for the last time."

The other candidates on the Student List range from academics to athletes – and economists to engineers. None of them has a political background. But the students who selected them believe that is a strength, rather than a weakness.

"We've gathered people who are actually the best in their fields, and we really think that they are competent enough to rule the country," says Aleksandra, a student at Novi Sad University who only wants to give her first name.

"All of them are gathered around the same vision of a country where the freedom of speech is ruling, where you can walk to your home in the middle of the night and you will not be beaten up by some hooligans," she adds.

The Student List and its supporters say that Aleksandar Vučić and the SNS dominate state institutions and media coverage.

At the last parliamentary election in 2023, the International Election Observation Mission noted "overwhelming ruling party advantage" due to "bias in the media" and "misuse of public office and resources".

The BBC approached leading figures in the SNS for an interview but was not offered a response.

For the past 18 months, there has also been a full-time, pro-SNS camp in the small park between the National Assembly and the Presidency building in the centre of Belgrade. Its residents have repeatedly attacked journalists and made the park a no-go zone for local people.

Vučić has called the camp "a symbol of resistance" against those who "cannot stand different opinions".

But his major challenge remains what happened outside Novi Sad railway station two years ago.

The station's renovation was a key part of his signature infrastructure project – the high-speed line linking Belgrade and Budapest. So it has been difficult for Vučić to distance himself from the disaster.

Protests followed, with participants accusing the authorities of corruption and having "blood on their hands".

"This is a problem for the government," says Magda Anastasijevic, the Eastern Europe analyst for the conflict monitor, ACLED.

"Vučić has survived this in the past, he was always able to find a scapegoat and blame whatever problems on them. This was not the case for the canopy."

On the diplomatic front, he has performed a delicate balancing act.

Membership talks with the EU continue, albeit fitfully, even as Serbia retains close ties with Russia and China – both countries that refuse to recognise Kosovo's unilateral declaration of independence from Serbia.

Vučić has warned those links could be severed if the Student List took power.

"When you ask them: will you impose sanctions on Russia? Silence, umming and ah-ing, but no answer," he told the audience at a pre-election rally.

"You know what the Chinese think, you've heard what Vladimir Putin said. So you decide. Think about who has our best interests at heart."

The final rallies of the campaign saw the SNS stage an event at Belgrade Arena, with Aleksandar Vučić as the only speaker. But on the other side of the Sava River, the Student List attracted a reported 150,000 people in Slavija Square to listen to a mixture of students and candidates.

The contrasting visions were clear to see: the strong, sole leader – or a collective approach. Now Serbia's electorate must decide which they prefer.

images.caption: The Student List is Number 3 on Serbia's ballot paper, so the figure seen being hugged by this supporter has become a symbol of the movement's fight for change

articles.title: Jazzy: The Irish DJ dropping her debut after a billion streams
articles.summary: Irish DJ Jazzy came up on the Dublin club scene and has worked with industry heavyweights like Calvin Harris.
articles.body:
Releasing your first album is a big step for any artist, but for Jazzy it's one that's followed some huge strides.

The Irish singer and DJ has been streamed more than a billion times and worked with industry heavyweights including Calvin Harris.

If that's not enough, on Saturday she has her biggest gig yet when she'll be playing tracks like No Bad Vibes and Someday in front of a home crowd in Dublin.

For Jazzy, writing an album has always been in the back of her mind and now, finally, it's time to hit send.

She's previously released dozens of singles, building up a monthly listenership over 10 million strong, but Peace and Patience is her first full-length work.

"It's been quite a few years of creating some smaller projects," she tells BBC Newsbeat.

"That's given me enough experience now to feel like it was the right moment."

The 30-year-old, real name Yasmine Byrne, has been putting out music for more than five years and collabed with the likes of Sonny Fodera, Rossi. and KILIMANJARO on some of her biggest tracks.

Dance music has boomed in recent years, with Spotify previously telling Newsbeat that since 2020 the amount under-25s listen to the genre has grown by more than 73% globally.

It also dominated festival line-ups over the summer - including Radio 1's Big Weekend which dedicated all its stages to dance music on the opening night.

But artists in the genre have often moved away from albums, opting instead to release EPs and singles.

Jazzy has noticed the change, saying it feels "a lot different now, with people kind of siding with virality rather than quality of music".

"When I was making the album, I wasn't thinking about going viral or anything like that. I just wanted to make something that was true to me and sounded like a Jazzy album.

"I like to let things happen quite organically and I try to just let the music speak to me."

Jazzy is rooted in the Dublin club scene, starting her career as part of a group called Powerful Creative Minds in the city.

But as more and more clubs close, the DJ says there are fewer opportunities for artists to cut their teeth offline.

"When I first started going out, there was a lot more going on," she says.

"There was a lot more nightclubs to go to and it's very different when we look at it now, which is sad.

"There's definitely a home for dance music on the internet of course but club culture is very important and I think that's something that we need to keep going for sure."

Latest figures from the Night Time Industries Association suggest about 12 venues are closing across the UK every month, with almost 30% of the night time economy lost since the coronavirus pandemic.

"I hope to God that it doesn't disappear, the club scene altogether," says Jazzy, who describes a similar issue in Ireland.

"We all need to try and put a hand in to keep it going."

Jazzy's taking her new album on tour across the UK from next month, but first she has her biggest gig yet: Dublin's 3Arena in front of a home crowd.

Even after a Coachella set and supporting Calvin Harris, she describes this as the "biggest milestone of my career to date".

While she says fans can mostly expect her brand of uplifting records on the album, she says it's also more personal than her usual work.

She highlights one track in particular, Invisible, as a change from her more upbeat releases. It deals with a bad experience she had in the music industry, describing it as "like my first ever diss track".

"I hope [fans] learn a little bit more about me, because that was one of my goals with the album - to open up a little bit about experiences in life as well.

"So there's a little message from me in each song."

articles.title: Typhoon Champi hits Taiwan, killing one and injuring hundreds
articles.summary: Authorities warn of ‘destructive winds’ and urge residents to shelter as the storm passes the island’s northeast.
articles.body:
Typhoon Champi has struck Taiwan, killing one person and injuring at least 350 others, as authorities warned of “destructive winds” and instructed people to stay indoors.

The storm swept past the island’s northeast on Friday, toppling trees, shutting shops and schools, cutting power to thousands of households, and forcing more than 4,300 people to evacuate from their homes.

Champi is heading towards China and Japan, forcing the cancellation of hundreds of flights in the region.

“From tonight through tomorrow morning conditions will be very windy and stormy everywhere,” Central Weather Administration (CWA) forecaster Lin Ping-yu said in a briefing. “Please try to stay indoors.”

Champi was briefly a super typhoon with winds of nearly 300 kilometres per hour (186 miles per hour) but has since weakened. The US Joint Typhoon Warning Center reported maximum winds of 185km/h (115mph).

Worse is still expected to come on Saturday. Champi could drop up to 900mm (35 inches) of rain between Thursday and Saturday, with the northeast hit hardest, the CWA said. More than 400mm fell in Yilan County on Friday.

CWA forecaster Lu Kuo-chen said the typhoon could slow near the island’s northeastern tip, prolonging its impact.

About 8,400 households in Japan’s Okinawa islands were without power on Friday afternoon, according to the Okinawa Electric Power Company. Champi is forecast to hover near Okinawa and then China’s eastern coast before turning northeast towards mainland Japan.

Champi is the latest storm in a Pacific season supercharged by El Nino.

The United Nations said on Wednesday that El Nino, a natural cycle that warms the tropical Pacific, is heading off the charts.

“The current El Nino event could be unprecedented in strength. Literally off the monitoring charts that we have used for the past four decades,” said Celeste Saulo, secretary-general of the World Meteorological Organization.

It is expected to peak in December, with its impact lasting into 2027 and beyond.

articles.title: Are California voters about to impose world's first tax on billionaires?
articles.summary: Voters are about to decide if the mega-rich among them should hand over billions of dollars to pay for improvements to healthcare.
articles.body:
Few places on the planet have as many ultra-wealthy residents as California, a US state known for glamour, coastal mega-mansions and being home to many rich and famous.

Now voters are about to decide if the mega-rich among them - names that include media mogul Oprah Winfrey, Meta head Mark Zuckerberg, Skims cofounder and reality television star Kim Kardashian and filmmaker George Lucas - should hand over billions of dollars to pay for improvements to healthcare.

Proposition 40 is aimed at levying a one-time 5% tax on the net worth of all of California's billionaires.

There are a little more than 200 such individuals in the state - but that hasn't stopped the measure from dividing leaders and causing some of its ultra-wealthy residents to flee. One billionaire businessman says he's brought jobs to California, but the proposition made him feel "a little bit like I wasn't wanted".

What are the US midterms? A simple guide

But the vote is also offering regular everyday residents a voice on an issue that has riled politics for decades.

"I believe this is the first billionaire tax - meaning a wealth tax that is targeting a very extreme percentile of the wealth distribution," says Francesco Trebbi, a public policy professor at the University of California, Berkeley. He noted the measure's historic nature and how it could help even out California's wealth gap.

The state has the largest economy in the country - and boasts the fourth largest global economy, bigger than India and the whole of the UK. And it is home to one of the highest concentrations of billionaires in the globe. But it also has the largest share of homeless people in the nation and one of the highest wealth gaps.

Those who back the measure have argued it helps ensure that the ultra-wealthy are contributing their fair share and will help backfill gaps in the state's budget. The move aims to raise $100bn (£75bn) to make up for federal funding cuts to the state's health-care system.

Suzanne Jimenez, chief of staff for Service Employees International Union-United Healthcare Workers West, which helped lead the charge for the initiative, says the measure is a "short-term solution" for massive federal funding cuts coming to California as a result of President Donald Trump's sweeping tax and spending bill .

"If we do nothing, we're going to see a collapse of our healthcare system, while we figure out a longer-term solution to fund our healthcare," she told the BBC.

While the ballot measure has many supporters - including some billionaires like Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang - it has faced fierce opposition from a variety of figures, from billionaires to the state's liberal governor.

Google co-founder Sergey Brin has given more than $100 million to a political nonprofit funding ballot measures that could block the wealth tax, the Los Angeles Times reports .

California Governor Gavin Newsom, whose tenure is coming to an end, is perhaps the most notable political leader opposing it. He has voiced concerns that the measure could cause the wealthy to leave the state and drive out their crucial income tax revenue.

A September poll from the Berkeley Institute of Governmental Studies and the Los Angeles Times found the proposition has not clearly won over a majority of voters, with 45% of likely voters in favour of the tax, 42% opposed and 13% undecided.

The statewide ballot measure would need to be approved by a majority of residents.

California is not the first place to toy with the idea of taxing the rich. Also on the West Coast, voters in US state of Washington are considering whether to accept or reject a "millionaires tax" - a 9.9% tax on income over $1m a year.

While wealth taxes were once a fairly common form of taxation in Europe, they have rapidly fallen out of favour and now only exist in three European countries – Spain, Norway and Switzerland, says Dr Kristian Niemietz, head of political economy at the Institute of Economic Affairs.

Niemietz believes wealth taxes are "more trouble than they are worth" because they cause administrative issues, suppress investment, lead to capital flight and, in the end, do not raise much revenue, she said.

In the case of Norway, a local news organisation found that an increase in the wealth tax led to more super wealthy people leaving the country in 2022 than in the preceding 13 years combined. A study on Switzerland found that a 0.1 percentage point increase in a wealth tax reduced taxable wealth by 3.5%.

The California measure, if approved, would apply retroactively to those with a net worth of at least $1bn who resided in California as of 1 January 2026. At least six of the state's 200 plus billionaires have reportedly left California ahead of that deadline to avoid the tax.

They include Google co-founders Larry Page and Sergey Brin, venture capitalist Peter Thiel, former Uber CEO Travis Kalanick and Hankey Group founder Don Hankey.

Hankey, a Los Angeles billionaire who has lived in California all his life, told Forbes he left for the state of Nevada as a result of the proposed wealth tax.

"I think we've created a lot of jobs in California. We have a few thousand people working for us and we have a profit sharing plan. And I have to leave the state," he added, saying the measure made him feel like he wasn't "wanted" in the state.

Meta chief executive Mark Zuckerberg told the company's board last month that he was thinking of moving his primary residence out of California over the proposed tax. To prevent him from leaving the state - where the company is headquartered - Meta agreed to a new stock deal that gives Zuckerberg, whose wealth is estimated to exceed $200bn, even more shares in the company to make up for the billions he would lose if the measure passes in November. Estimates say he could owe as much as $12.5bn.

DoorDash cofounder Andy Fang, who has an estimated net worth of $1.6bn, has called the measure "stupid" and wrote on X that "proposals like this make it irresponsible for me not to plan leaving the state".

Zuckerberg wins Meta deal to help him foot bill for possible California billionaire tax

Meanwhile, businessman Tom Steyer, who ran an unsuccessful bid for California governor earlier this year, is one of the few billionaires who has said he would vote in favour of the tax. Steyer said that although he believes the way the measure is written is "problematic", it is necessary to protect vulnerable Californians.

Huang, too, has expressed support of paying the levy.

"I don't mind paying taxes. The more you make, the more taxes you pay. I'm okay with that," the Nvidia chief executive said in an interview with the BBC's news partner in the US, CBS. "I am the ultimate American Dream."

Senator Bernie Sanders of Vermont, a vocal champion against income inequality, has campaigned in support of Prop 40.

While at a Los Angeles rally, Sanders said billionaires "believe, like the monarchs of the 19th century, that they have a God-given right to rule".

"They have all the wealth; they got all the power, and who the hell do you think you are challenging them? Well, I think on Nov 3 they're going to learn a very powerful lesson".

Income inequality in the US is at some of its highest levels in over three decades, with the top 1% of households owning nearly 32% of all US wealth in the third quarter of 2025. It is also near historic highs in California.

Economic inequality is a concern among most Californians, with 72% believing that the gap between the rich and poor is widening and a similar share holding that state government should do more to reduce the gap, according to a statewide survey from the Public Policy Institute of California.

Trebbi says it is an "anti-elite, anti-system sentiment that is behind a policy" like Prop 40.

"This is really not about Prop 40," he says. It's about trying to "re-balance the scale a little bit".

articles.title: Strictly Come Dancing's new hosts: Flat-footed or fab-u-lous?
articles.summary: Josh Widdicombe, Emma Willis and Johannes Radebe have split opinion but are getting into the groove, critics say.
articles.body:
Strictly Come Dancing's new hosting trio received a very mixed reception when the latest series began a month ago. Ratings have dipped and the jury's still out, but critics say they are slowly getting into the groove.

Changing the hosting team on the BBC's flagship Saturday night entertainment show was never likely to be a waltz in the park.

And going from two presenters to three, and giving them slightly different roles, upset the show's rhythm even more.

Tess Daly and Claudia Winkleman were always going to be a hard act to follow.

Into their sparkly shoes have stepped the safe and smooth Emma Willis; the flamboyant former professional dancer Johannes Radebe; and cheeky comedian Josh Widdicombe, a wildcard who was not hitherto associated with either the dance world or prime-time TV.

Willis and Widdicombe have been paired on the live shows, where he is tasked with injecting humour into the moments before and after each dance - with mixed results, say critics.

Radebe, meanwhile, has taken over from Winkleman upstairs on the mezzanine, bringing his warmth and dance expertise to the celebrity interviews following each routine.

After they made their debuts in September, the Times' Carol Midgley billed them as "TV's most awkward ménage à trois".

The Daily Telegraph's Chris Bennion declared that Strictly's "new 'throuple' is an utter disaster", adding: "It's a mess, a muddle, a confusing pudding".

Widdicombe has come in for particular flack. He "felt like an awkward spare part" and looked like "the work experience boy", wrote Sasha Morris of the Daily Express .

And the Independent's Isobel Lewis said Widdicombe "is a problem the show needs to solve".

She believes things have now improved, although the show hasn't completely solved the problem.

"He's basically acting too much like a comedian to be a presenter," the freelance culture journalist tells BBC News.

"I think he's getting more comfortable with it. When it's him and Emma doing the bits when they intro each act, and they're obviously reading off an autocue, they feel way more confident there, and it feels more like it works."

The problem grows when Widdicombe does what comes naturally as a good comedian, Lewis says, and tries to be spontaneous.

"They've got, like, 20 seconds with each judge. It's such a tight amount of time, and that's what lends it to feeling sloppy and like he's constantly jumping in.

"Unfortunately it reads a bit like trying to steal attention and have the last laugh. I actually don't think that is what he's trying to do as a selfish act. I just think that is his comedic impulse."

She says it's unfair to put the criticism on Widdicombe, and says as time has gone on he feels less awkward, with comments online suggesting some fans are "warming to him".

"But at the beginning there's always that knee-jerk reaction of, 'I don't like this'," Lewis says.

Radio Times TV and podcast editor Caroline Frost agrees that the trio have gradually settled in.

"I think it's fair to say there were some bumps in the road in the first couple of episodes," she says, "but they do appear to be very slowly relaxing into their new roles."

When it comes to Willis and Widdicombe's double act, Frost would like to see more spontaneity, not less.

"They've been relying quite visibly on scripts and gags, and I would like to see them relax into themselves," she adds.

"It's completely understandable that they would be very scripted, very alert to the clock and to all of the other many demands of running a live show of that scale - but the really talented people can do that on the fly.

"Josh is very likeable, and we know he's a very funny man," she notes. "He doesn't need the shackles of the script that he's currently handcuffed to, and I would love to see him take off those cuffs and become more spontaneous."

Frost suggests sending Widdicombe upstairs to conduct the post-dance interviews instead of Radebe, who at times struggles to control his exuberant former fellow dancers. "It's a bit like when you get an internal promotion at work," she reflects.

The producers should make the most of Radebe's strengths and make him "a sort of talent pundit", she suggests.

"Have him in the rehearsal rooms, telling us what's going on. He would be a lovely middleman between what we're seeing on the dance floor and what is going on technically."

Ahead of the series, there had been reports that Radebe would be used as a "roving reporter".

Widdicombe previously suggested the trio's roles would be fluid, telling The Rest Is Entertainment it was "going to be like total football... We're going to be moving everywhere".

But while some segments are flexible - especially in the Sunday result show - their main roles appear fixed.

Some fans have been won over by Radebe since he took over Winkleman's old domain.

"JoJo has been really brilliant up in... I guess the Claudatorium, but I'm not sure what we call it now," says Flo Sayers, co-host of the Strictly on the Sofa podcast.

"He is the link to previous Strictly, and I think he has taken to that role really well. I like that he's a bit different from Claudia. He's less the comedian and more the supportive friend for the contestants when they've got off the dance floor and they're probably feeling a little bit vulnerable.

"And his fashion has been amazing, so I'm excited to see what he wears every week."

Sayers isn't sure whether the new line-up has contributed to lower ratings - about six million people are tuning in every week this year, down by about a million.

But overall, she believes that the trio are getting used to the demands of the series.

Dr Karen Wood, associate professor at the Centre for Dance Research at Coventry University, agrees and says the trio "are now really starting to feel a bit more settled".

"I think JoJo has transitioned beautifully from professional dancer to host, and obviously he comes with all his fabulousness," she says.

"He's able to talk about the technical details as well as be very supportive to the professional dancers and the celebrities. And his outfits are just marvellous. So I think he suits that role very well.

"Likewise, Emma is holding her own when she's with Josh and when she's not. She's an experienced presenter. You can you can tell.

"And Josh is bringing the humour. I know it's come with some criticism. But last week was the first week that I felt, oh, these two are actually funny."

She concludes: "It's really feeling like they're finding their stride and their rhythm with it. And I think that's going to develop more and more - very much as the celebrities do."

Just as the show's celebrity contestants improve week by week, the same may be true of the hosts - except viewers can't vote them off if they don't like them.

The next episode of Strictly Come Dancing airs on BBC One at 18:30 BST on Saturday.

articles.title: Rubio urges Cubans to work with CIA to bring political change to communist-run island
articles.summary: Secretary of State Marco Rubio urged Cubans to form a "discrete partnership with the CIA" as Trump floated sending him to Cuba to cut a deal.
articles.body: Secretary of State Marco Rubio urged Cubans seeking political change Friday to discreetly cooperate with the CIA as President Donald Trump separately floated sending Rubio to the communist-run island to negotiate a deal. "To those who seek to create positive change in Cuba - now is the time," Rubio wrote in a post on X. "The disappointment of failed promises, corruption, and the privileged lives of only a few; seize this opportunity to create the change you desire through a discrete partnership with the CIA." RUBIO WARNS CUBA HAS INFILTRATED US WITH SPIES, CALLS COMMUNIST REGIME AN 'ESPIONAGE SUPERPOWER' Rubio's message explicitly encouraged Cubans to work with the U.S. intelligence agency but did not identify a specific operation or explain what such cooperation would involve. Rubio, the son of Cuban immigrants, has long advocated for a tougher U.S. approach toward the Cuban government. The former Florida senator has been a prominent critic of the communist leadership in Havana and opposed efforts to normalize relations without political reforms. Trump, meanwhile, raised the possibility of U.S. ships stopping near Cuba while discussing Iran during a midterm rally in Fort Myers, Florida, Friday. TRUMP EXPANDS CUBA SANCTIONS BEYOND US COMPANIES IN MAJOR CRACKDOWN ON FOREIGN ENABLERS "Don't worry. We'll take care of Cuba on our way back from Iran with it. We'll do a little stopover now. We'll do a little stopover," Trump told the crowd. "Actually, what we're going to do with Cuba is we're going to come back from Iran. Those beautiful ships will pass Cuba. We'll have one of them stop about 50 yards off the coast. They'll raise up their hands." Trump then suggested Rubio could handle negotiations with the communist-run island. IRANIAN NEGOTIATORS KICKED OUT OF US AS TALKS STALL, TRUMP LAYS OUT 'POSSIBLE' TIMELINE FOR MORE STRIKES "And then we're going to send Marco Rubio in to finish up the deal. We'll have Marco. Marco. We don't even have to stop. We could just put him in there and he'll figure it out. He's a great guy." Trump did not provide details about any proposed agreement with Cuba or indicate whether his remarks reflected an actual military or diplomatic plan. articles.title: How to heat your home without turning on the heating
articles.summary: Make draught excluders from socks, leave your oven door open after cooking and opt for lots of thin layers of clothing to stay warm.
articles.body:
As the UK braces for a chilly weekend, with powerful winds and heavy rain hitting parts of the country, people are looking for ways to bring some warmth to their homes without cranking up the heating just yet. It is autumn after all.

But with rising energy prices making heating homes more expensive, taking action now could pay off in the long run.

Experts warn, though, that if you're elderly or vulnerable you shouldn't compromise your health.

To help you prepare for the chillier months, BBC News asked families and experts to share their tips for keeping your home warm and cost-effective.

Eat hearty winter meals to warm you through

When it gets cold, many people turn to hot water bottles and blankets - but there are other ways to warm your body.

The British Heart Foundation recommends wearing lots of thin layers, rather than one thick layer, to trap the heat in.

Natalie, 29, says she's replaced some of the clothes she wears round the house with supermarket thermal leggings and tops and says "it's made such a difference".

Amber Waring, 27, from Devon, says she eats warm meals like stews and pasta bakes, and dances round the kitchen with her toddler while they cook to help keep warm.

With the clocks going back this weekend, the nights will be drawing in.

So if you have a thicker duvet, now is the time to bring it out. Some supermarkets sell winter duvets for under £20 - look for 10.5 tog or higher.

But there's something to be said for a craftily placed blanket, too. When it gets cold, Rebecca, 44, from Hertfordshire, sleeps with a blanket underneath her mattress, which she says stops draughts. "This was passed to me by my nan, she swore by it," she says. Others swear by placing a blanket above the mattress but under the bedsheet.

You can heat your bed before getting in with a hot water bottle, but make sure you check the expiry date. A guide by NHS Scotland says to let the water from the kettle cool for a few minutes before filling, only fill it two-thirds full, squeeze air out of the top before putting the stopper on, and don't hold it directly against your skin.

Using an electric blanket - to heat your bed before you get in or to wrap around yourself on the sofa - is "one of the cheapest ways" to stay warm, says Emily Seymour, energy editor at consumer organisation Which?. Testing by Which? shows it typically costs between 2p and 8p an hour to run an electric blanket at its highest setting. The London Fire Brigade says to unplug your blanket before you get into bed unless it has a thermostat control, not to use a hot water bottle at the same time, and replace it every 10 years.

Open curtains and let the sun in during the day

Keep doors closed to trap heat in the room you're in. You can place curtains or blankets over your doors for extra insulation.

Embrace the daylight. "If it's sunny outside, open the curtains so the sun heats the room, then shut them when the sun sets to keep the heat in," says Rebecca.

"If you're using a hot appliance, let the heat into the room," says Lianne Macfarlane, 40, from Cheshire. She recommends leaving your oven door open after using it to help warm your kitchen, though this isn't advised if you have small children who could injure themselves.

As well as curtains, other soft furnishings like rugs can help keep a room warm, says Seymour.

If you have a fireplace, lighting a fire to warm the room you're in can be cheaper than turning on the central heating for your whole house. Elin Davis, 30, from South Wales, says her log burner is more economical than turning her heating on - though she added that "logs can cost quite a bit these days".

Gaps around doors can cause heat to escape, so place draught excluders around your door frames. You don't need to buy them - you can use towels or stuff socks into a pair of tights.

When it's a windy day, Seymour recommends looking for other draughts in your house and either finding ways to seal these spots yourself or calling in a professional to help. These include using foam strips, sealant and specialist chimney draught excluders if you don't use your fireplace. Things such as extractor fans and purpose-built ventilation shouldn't be blocked, she adds.

If your windows are single-glazed, then Sophie Burr of charity National Energy Action suggests looking at secondary glazing or investing in thermal curtains to help keep the heat in. Or for a cheaper option, some people suggest placing bubble wrap on your windows.

Even though it may be tempting, don't keep your windows closed all the time. Seymour notes that it's important to allow some ventilation in your house to prevent damp.

"I wouldn't recommend not having your heating on at all," says Seymour, pointing to both the health issues this can cause as well as how pipes can freeze over.

But there are ways you can use heating wisely. These include checking whether your energy supplier offers cheaper prices at off-peak times, bleeding your radiators so that they're more efficient, and turning your heating up in small increments until you reach the right temperature. If you have furniture in front of your radiator, then try moving it to avoid blocking the heat.

You can also buy dedicated radiator foil or make your own with kitchen foil to reflect the heat back into the room rather than losing it through the walls, says Burr. She points out that about 35% of heat that comes from radiators is lost through walls.

Cora Harrison, 34, from Wakefield, says that she only turns the radiators on in the rooms her family is using and keeps the heating on at a low level when they're on holiday to avoid mould or pipes bursting. Some radiators have a snowflake symbol on the valve that activates the frost protection setting, meaning that if the room gets very cold, the radiator warms slightly to stop the pipes from bursting.

Another way to potentially reduce energy bills is to lower the flow temperature of your combi boiler. If you book a boiler service, an engineer can do this for you.

You can also find free warm spaces such as libraries and community centres in your area by looking online or contacting the council. Some spaces also provide free hot drinks.

Household energy prices are set to soar in January, with a typical bill expected to jump by £276 a year, according to a forecast last month from consultancy Cornwall Insight. The 16% predicted increase would mark the biggest rise for four years.

Rising bills are "particularly concerning for people with kids, people with health conditions and the elderly," says Emily Jeremy, project manager at Manchester South Central Foodbank.

An estimated 9.4% of households in England lived in fuel poverty in 2025, according to the latest government figures .

Rodney Winchester, 65, from Thetford, who spoke to BBC News through the charity Christians Against Poverty, says he's "extremely worried" about rising energy prices. Because of health conditions, he says he has to keep the heating on throughout winter but is concerned he won't be able to afford it.

"It's so scary," Rodney says, adding that he's been cutting back on food spending and keeps getting ill in the cold weather.

If you are struggling with prices, the debt charity StepChange recommends checking whether you qualify for any additional support, like the Warm Home Discount and Winter Fuel Payment. It also advises contacting your energy supplier, which may be able to agree an affordable repayment plan or discuss support schemes.

articles.title: Tyler Robinson hearing ends without trial date set, prompting fiery plea from Erika Kirk's lawyer
articles.summary: Tyler Robinson's Utah trial for the assassination of Charlie Kirk still has no start date as prosecutors and defense attorneys clash over timing.
articles.body: PROVO, Utah — Tyler Robinson, the 23-year-old Utah man accused of assassinating Charlie Kirk at a Turning Point USA event last year, still doesn't have a trial date after a Utah judge listened to oral arguments from both sides — and a lawyer for Kirk's widow — about how much time they think they'll need and when they'd like to start. Robinson, wearing a light gray suit, uncuffed and unshackled, did not address the court. He spoke quietly with attorneys Richard Novak, Kathy Nester and Staci Visser during breaks, at one point handing Visser a note. Judge Tony Graf Jr. said he had planned to set a trial date at the end of the hearing but needed more time after questioning both sides about their expected timelines and commitments in previously scheduled trials on other cases. Jeffrey Neiman, an attorney for Kirk's widow, Erika, pleaded with the court to speed things up. Robinson did not enter a plea until last month, nearly a year after being charged. LAWYERS FOR CHARLIE KIRK'S ACCUSED ASSASSIN TYLER ROBINSON WANT CAMERAS BANNED AFTER REPORT ON TAXPAYER BURDEN Justice delayed this long stops being justice for the Kirk family. "Every day of delay adds to uncertainty, invites speculation and that erodes confidence in this system," Neiman said at one point. The roughly three-hour hearing included several interruptions due to technical difficulties with WebEx, with Robinson defense attorney Michael Burt and an attorney for Kirk's parents, Robert and Kathy, attending remotely. Utah County prosecutors had floated Jan. 31, 2028, as their preferred trial date but said they could be ready in October 2027. TYLER ROBINSON TO FACE TRIAL IN CHARLIE KIRK ASSASSINATION AS JUDGE KEEPS DEATH PENALTY ON TABLE Visser said that pretrial litigation "builds upon itself," and given that there are over 31,000 pieces of discovery and "8 million" artifacts of digital evidence, lawyers will need time to file motions to compel, file subpoenas, etc. "Discovery review is foundational," she said. "It impacts everything else." As a result, she said, the state’s proposed January 2028 trial is "not practical." The defense had asked for a "soft target" date in the third quarter of 2029, citing large amounts of discovery and other trial preparations — as well as trial commitments in other cases. Among those, one directly conflicted with the prosecution's desired start date, a federal racketeering case defense attorney Novak has scheduled for Jan. 10, 2028. Both sides agreed that setting a trial that would run through the holidays could put potential jurors and witnesses in a bind. ERIKA KIRK PENS ESSAY ON GRIEF AS READERS GAIN INSIGHTS INTO WRENCHING PAST YEAR "Justice delayed this long stops being justice for the Kirk family," Neiman said. Neiman noted that only about 5% of federal cases actually make it to trial and said the Kirk family would be happy to write to the federal judge and ask for the January trial to be rescheduled to clear up Robinson's defense attorney. Under Utah's state constitution, victims and their representatives have a right to a speedy resolution to their case. Erika Kirk is the court's designated victim's representative. Novak told the court that the trial's start date had been "set in stone" and argued against rushing things along in the case against Robinson. "The reality is rushing to trial does not lead to closure. It does not lead to finality. It leads to mistakes," he said. UTAH PROSECUTORS ASK JUDGE TO SHUT DOWN DELAY TACTICS IN CHARLIE KIRK ASSASSINATION CASE Graf expressed concern that if he does not set a date soon, additional conflicts could arise. GOT A TIP? Neiman, who is primarily a criminal defense attorney, has repeatedly asked the court to speed things up. LISTEN TO THE NEW 'CRIME & JUSTICE WITH DONNA ROTUNNO' PODCAST "Time is the defense’s best ally," he said. "It’s their best friend." GET BREAKING NEWS BY EMAIL He also noted that, regardless of when the trial takes place, Charlie Kirk won't be able to spend Christmas with his family. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "Your honor, if you set it, it will happen," Neiman said. "Set it, please." Graf set the next hearing for Monday, Nov. 9 at 1 p.m. MT, when he said he would read his ruling.

articles.title: Woman, 65, becomes second patient to die of Ebola in Kenya
articles.summary: She was a close family member of the first victim, a man who had travelled from the Democratic Republic of Congo.
articles.body:
Kenya has recorded its second death from Ebola as it handles its first ever outbreak of the disease.

A woman, aged 65, who was a close family member of the first victim, a man who had travelled from the Democratic Republic of Congo, died after being placed in quarantine, the health ministry said.

Seven other Ebola patients were receiving treatment at two isolation facilities, it added.

All the cases were within "one cluster, with no evidence of community spread", the ministry said.

More than 4,000 people have died in Africa since Ebola was confirmed in DR Congo in May, making it the second most deadly outbreak of the disease.

Kenya's latest victim was a "direct contact and close family member of the first case (deceased) and was under quarantine when she developed symptoms" on 13 October, the health ministry said.

The first death, on 5 October, was that of a man who fell ill in September and was treated in several hospitals in DR Congo before arriving in the Kenyan capital, Nairobi, where he died a few days later.

Those still being treated are three other relatives of the first victim, three health workers and a hospital cleaner.

The US has warned its citizens against travelling to Kenya, while neighbouring countries such as Uganda, Ethiopia and Somalia are also on alert.

Ebola is a rare but deadly disease caused by a virus. As the disease progresses, vomiting and diarrhoea develop and it can lead to organ failure. Some, but not all, patients develop internal and external bleeding.

The disease spreads from one person to another by contact with infected bodily fluids such as blood or vomit.

The Bundibugyo species of Ebola is relatively rare, with no approved vaccine or treatment - though trials are under way.

With more than 9,500 cases in DR Congo, Kenya faces a steady risk of new cases arriving across borders, according to the International Rescue Committee, which has been working alongside both governments to contain the spread.

Kenya has introduced enhanced screening for travellers arriving from DR Congo and nine other countries it considers to be at high risk: Uganda, Tanzania, Rwanda, Burundi, Angola, Zambia, Ethiopia, South Sudan and the Central African Republic.

Travellers arriving from those countries are required to complete a digital surveillance form before boarding their flights, and to present a QR code to port health officials on arrival.

Kenya also ordered enhanced public health screening of aircraft arriving from those countries, as authorities seek to prevent further imported cases.

Within the country, the government has been sharing public messages to create awareness about Ebola, including encouraging people to promptly report any suspected cases and seek care at a hospital.

It has also focused on hygiene and safety measures, such as washing hands and avoiding close contact with sick people.

Is Ebola under control in Kenya after nine cases confirmed?

Woman with Ebola in Nigeria confirmed as wife of Swiss diplomat

'I buried my parents one day after the other' - Ebola mourners learn how to grieve safely

In another development, Nigeria's health minister has said the country's single confirmed case of Ebola appears to be genetically related to a strain identified earlier in Kenya.

Professor Ali Pate said there was no evidence so far that the Kenyan patient had travelled to Nigeria, but that further testing was under way.

He emphasised that Nigeria had so far recorded only one confirmed case of the virus.

"We are conducting additional tests. Some of the results are negative, while others are pending," Pate said.

Health officials have been investigating whether Nigeria's first case crossed paths with Kenya's first patient. Both are believed to have travelled through Uganda's Entebbe International Airport earlier this month.

articles.title: WHO announces start of Ebola vaccine clinical trial in DR Congo
articles.summary: A clinical trial begins to test the safety, efficacy and immunogenicity of multiple vaccines.
articles.body:
The World Health Organization (WHO) has announced the beginning of the first clinical trial of an Ebola vaccine in the outbreak that started in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC).

WHO’s director-general, Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, said in a social media post on Friday that participants in the trial were vaccinated with the Ervebo vaccine in Bunia, the capital of the DRC’s northeastern Ituri province, which is the epicentre of the Ebola outbreak.

Ervebo, a vaccine approved for use against the more common Zaire strain of Ebola, will be put through a full-scale human trial to see if it offers any cross-protection against the Bundibugyo species of Ebola that is behind the epidemic.

“This trial will help us understand whether any of the vaccine candidates designed for Bundibugyo virus work,” the WHO chief said on X.

“WHO is supporting this DRC-led effort to find answers and save lives,” he added.

The DRC declared its 17th and worst-ever Ebola outbreak in May and has since reported more than 9,700 cases, with the number of deaths exceeding 4,600.

The WHO, in response, triggered a public health emergency of international concern, its second-highest alert level.

The current outbreak has now been reported in four countries across eastern, central ⁠⁠and western Africa, giving it the widest geographic spread of any Ebola outbreak on the continent to date.

The so-called Tumaini trial is a single trial framework that can test the safety, efficacy and immunogenicity of multiple vaccines.

The trial will use a ring vaccination approach: immunising contacts deemed to be at high risk of infection.

The trial is set to incorporate two Bundibugyo-specific candidate vaccines, which are currently advancing through earlier-stage, smaller-scale clinical trials.

One is a ChAdOx1 adenoviral vector jab being developed by the University of Oxford; the other, by the US-based Moderna group, uses mRNA technology.

Both have received funding from the Coalition for Epidemic Preparedness Innovations and are expected to enter the trial “shortly”, CEPI said in a statement.

The trial will include pregnant women and children aged 12 years and older, generating evidence for populations that are often excluded from clinical trials.

WHO emergencies director Chikwe Ihekweazu said the trial was set up to generate the rigorous evidence needed to determine whether the participating vaccines could protect people at risk.
